clue.text: Work inside cold American plant

indicators.note: one piece sits within the pair of abbreviations that flank it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to act is to work or perform

explanation.surface: A plant from America that does its work in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny desert plant, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Member describing old article's distinctive smell

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A club member is writing about a distinctive smell in an old newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like telling a story, but here it means drawing round, so ARM goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a characteristic odour, often pleasant, so it is a synonym for a distinctive smell.

clue.text: First-class spinner having fine match

parts.note: a spinning top is a toy that spins
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a match gives a light

explanation.surface: A top-quality spin bowler in cricket has a good game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a bowler, which is the surface picture; here it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank, a synonym for first-class.

clue.text: Reticent engaging with German forger?

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a reticent person is shy
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A quiet person gets involved with a German counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter, but here it means one who forges metal, a blacksmith; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy can mean a blacksmith, who literally forges iron, so the pun on a faker is fair.

clue.text: Dean at bizarre church social event

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange or twisted, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean turns up at a strange church social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea dance is an afternoon gathering with dancing and tea, so it is an example of a social event.

clue.text: With good visibility in seaside resorts, there's no apparent danger

definitions.text: With good visibility in seaside resorts
definitions.meaning: read literally, the shoreline can be seen plainly with no fog
the idiom says it is safe to go ahead because nobody is watching

explanation.surface: A weather forecast for the beach doubles as a reassurance that it is safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means that nobody is around to see or stop you, so no danger appears; literally it describes a clear view of the shore.

clue.text: Following each one, despite everything

parts.note: after means following in time or order
all covers each one of a group

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on following each person regardless of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in spite of what has been said or happened, the same as despite everything.

clue.text: Prize in American lottery raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: A prize in a US lottery has been increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like an increased jackpot, but in a down light it turns DRAW upwards into WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something given for merit or success, a synonym for prize.

clue.text: Angry over promise to supply puzzle

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: cross means angry
to give your word is to make a promise

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about a promise to supply a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the very kind of word game being solved here, so it is an example of a puzzle.

clue.text: Flattering remark made by companion, we hear

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be judged by how it is said rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: a complement is something that goes with and completes another, a companion piece

explanation.surface: A friend says something flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words, one with E and one with I, are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliment is words of praise, so it is a synonym for a flattering remark.

clue.text: Member of the clergy heading off shortly

indicators.note: the word loses its head, meaning its first letter is taken off

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman will be setting off soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like leaving; it means CANON loses its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or in a little while, a synonym for shortly.

clue.text: Everyone taken in by half of hoofer's sensational advertising

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, as if swallowed

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: Everyone is fooled by a dancer's showy publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link but gives its own letters BY, which hold ALL; 'half of' keeps HOO from hoofer. A hoofer is slang for a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy publicity or fuss, so it means sensational advertising.

clue.text: Salad ingredient consumed by undergrad is healthy

indicators.note: the answer is eaten up inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A student eats a salad vegetable and stays healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' fits the salad picture but means the letters sit inside 'undergrad is healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery red root is often eaten raw in salads, so it is an example of a salad ingredient.

clue.text: Royal family associated with Germany originally

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: take the first letter, where the word originates

explanation.surface: A royal house had its origins in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the British royal family's German roots, the Hanoverians.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male monarch, so here the noun stands for a royal person.

clue.text: Female lover over in Rabat, a Romanian

indicators.note: the letters are turned over, so they run backwards
the letters needed are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman's sweetheart in Morocco's capital turns out to be Romanian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ATAROMANI from 'Rabat, a Romanian' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inamorata is the Italian-derived word for a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or mistress.

clue.text: Answer's way out

definitions.meaning: the answer to a problem or puzzle
a way out of a difficulty

explanation.surface: An answer is described as a means of escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is both the answer to a question and a means of getting out of a difficulty.

clue.text: Under strain, guide high-flier up for trial?

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: to test something is to strain it or put it under stress
to pilot is to steer or guide

explanation.surface: Under pressure, someone steers an ambitious person towards a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up for trial' suggests a court case; the question mark flags that this flyer is literally aloft trying out new aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft to try them out, so is literally a flier high up on trial.

clue.text: Opera fairs badly in China?

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: china means mate or pal, from rhyming slang china plate

indicators.note: the word fairs is treated badly, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An opera does poorly when performed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but china plate is British rhyming slang for mate; 'badly' gives RSIFA.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is the last opera by Wagner, so it is an example of an opera.

clue.text: Smoked beef over rye, initially given to French friend

parts.note: something over is finished, past

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: ami is the French for friend

explanation.surface: A deli sandwich order: smoked beef on rye bread, served to a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over rye' looks like the deli order, but 'over' gives PAST and only the R of rye is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked cured beef, so it is an example of smoked beef.

clue.text: Fizzy drink accordingly put next to prosecutor

parts.note: so means therefore or accordingly
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink is duly placed beside the prosecutor in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is carbonated water or a sweet carbonated drink, so it is a fizzy drink.

clue.text: Relish (foremost of relishes) in small dish

parts.note: a relish is a condiment such as a sauce

indicators.note: only the foremost, or first, letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A condiment is served in a little bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small shallow dish, especially one set under a cup.

clue.text: Lots of strips of pasta needing no introduction

indicators.note: the word drops its introduction, meaning its first letter

parts.note: noodles are long thin strips of pasta

explanation.surface: Plenty of pasta ribbons that need no introducing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' sounds like praise for the dish; it removes the first letter N of NOODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, a synonym for lots.

clue.text: Tree with large span

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
an arch spans a gap, as a bridge does

explanation.surface: A tree whose branches spread widely.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Best player's back

definitions.meaning: the winner or title-holder in a sport
to back a cause is to support or stand up for it

explanation.surface: The top player has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is both the title-winning competitor and, as a verb, to support or argue for a cause.

clue.text: Love new tune being broadcast

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A new love song is being played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is going out live, so it is being broadcast.

clue.text: Piano tune for two

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A piano piece written as a duet for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two, so it means two.

clue.text: The head after tongue — what to put it on, once sliced?

definitions.text: what to put it on, once sliced?

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: French is a tongue, or language
loaf is slang for the head, as in use your loaf

explanation.surface: Cold tongue, the meat, served on bread slices: what to put it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' is both the meat in the surface and the language in the wordplay; 'it' in the definition is that sliced meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long crusty baguette is bread you might slice and lay sliced meat on, so it is where the tongue goes.

clue.text: One who's never met his match?

definitions.text: One who's never met his match?

parts.words: One who's never met his match?
parts.note: a match here is a marriage partner rather than an equal rival, so this man has never wed

explanation.surface: Praise for a man who has never been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never met his match' usually means unbeaten; the question mark flags that 'match' is a wedding match.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man has never found his spouse, so the idiom fits him literally.

clue.text: Stop working in retreat

definitions.meaning: to give up one's job at the end of a career
to withdraw or fall back, as an army does

explanation.surface: Leaving work after a career, while withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is both to give up work for good and to withdraw or fall back from a place.
